primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: On successful completion of a pretrial diversion programme the charges are dismissed, and the person may then petition for expunction of the public records where the charges were dismissed as a result of that successful completion. A petition is required; expunction is not automatic.
Bars expunction where the diverted offence was a sexual offence or a violent sexual offence as defined by the registration statute.
Requires the appropriate clerk's fee, so unlike a straight dismissal this route is not free.
The pretrial diversion scheme under which prosecution is suspended by memorandum of understanding with the district attorney general; the person does not plead guilty and is not found guilty.

The certificate requirement, which applies on this route because the exemption for expunctions under the non-conviction section is carved back where the expunction resulted from successful completion of diversion.

counselFlags: Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it.

No official Tennessee participant form exists. Both state form indices were inspected directly and neither publishes an expunction form of any kind; this is a negative finding established from the authoritative index, not a failure to search. A controlled custom instrument is therefore the only available strategy, and it is not represented as an official form.

Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025 and codified by Public Chapter 608 effective 2026-03-25, and clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering — the state's own expunction page still reasons from a section that has been nothing but definitions since 2025-04-24. A petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet carries the current citation and instructs the participant to confirm it with the clerk or the district attorney general before filing.
Tennessee expunction reaches no federal, military, tribal or out-of-state record, and a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on a clearance check.

The governing section prescribes no caption form and no contents for the participant's instrument. The caption follows the ordinary criminal-case style of the court having jurisdiction, with the filer designated as the source designates them. What individual clerks and courts in fact expect is not established and no county practice was surveyed; the caption is a visual- and counsel-review item.

A petition is still required after diversion. Completing diversion dismisses the case but leaves it visible until a separate petition is filed; the source records this as the second most common Tennessee misunderstanding.

This route is not free, which is the asymmetry a participant must be warned about: diversion is a non-conviction outcome, but a straight dismissal is free and this is not. The amount is set by a separate fee statute whose current text was not retrievable from an official source, so no figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The widely circulated figure appears only on a superseded page and does not appear in the enacted text.

A sexual offence or violent sexual offence as defined by the registration statute can be diverted but cannot be expunged. A person can complete diversion on such an offence and still be unable to clear the record, and the packet says so plainly rather than selling a petition.

The certificate from the state bureau is required on this route and an order must not be entered without it. It is a court instrument completed by court staff; this packet does not generate it, complete it, or assert it has been obtained.

The order is marked to the suspension-of-prosecution provision for a pretrial diversion case, which is how the bureau records it. That marking is part of the court's instrument, not the participant's.

No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears in the reorganized sections. The bureau operates an unpublished indigency procedure for its own separate certificate fee, using a form signed by the judge that it supplies on request and does not publish; that reaches the certificate fee and not the clerk's fee. No waiver mechanism for the clerk's fee was identified.

The enacted text uses two different ranges for the pretrial diversion scheme within one act. Whether that is a scrivener's error, and whether codification corrected it, was not established. It does not change which programme is meant, but it bears on which citation a petition should carry, and it is a recorded open question.

The state control number is a manual-completion item read from the participant's own criminal history. It stays a bracket in generated output; the order cannot be completed without it, and the participant is told to capture it early.

The shared renderer's fixed section heading "VI. VERIFICATION" is a Pennsylvania-derived artefact of the frozen renderer contract, not a Tennessee drafting choice. Nothing in the governing section requires verification. This is a visual- and counsel-review item.
No fee figure is quoted anywhere in this packet. The source records no retrievable amount, and the filing-fee field is left null rather than filled with a circulating number.
No fee-waiver instrument is included and the fee-waiver field is left null, because the source establishes no waiver mechanism for this route.
The governing section states no waiting period. None is pleaded, none is imported from a neighbouring section, and the waiting-period field is left null.

Notarization is not prescribed by the governing section and no verification statute exists to cite, so verificationStatute.citation is left null and the signature block carries no penalty citation. County practice may differ, and the packet directs the participant to ask the clerk.

Self-help stop conditions: Any dispute with the district attorney general about eligibility, or any indication the office will oppose. Any other conviction anywhere on the record, including federal and out-of-state convictions that would be ineligible in Tennessee. Unpaid court costs, fines or restitution, which mean the sentence is not complete. Any DUI, sexual offence or registration matter. Any domestic violence or child-victim offence. Federal, military, tribal or out-of-state records, which Tennessee expunction does not reach. Immigration consequences, and any security-clearance question. Any question that turns on whether the county clerk uses the pre-2025 or the reorganized section numbering. The offence was a sexual offence or a violent sexual offence as defined in T.C.A. § 40-39-202. It could be diverted but it cannot be expunged, and the participant needs to be told that plainly rather than sold a petition. The diversion was not successfully completed, or completion is disputed. The participant's goal involves federal employment or a security clearance, since a judicial diversion guilty plea may remain visible there.

provenance.registryExcerpt: Prosecution is suspended under a memorandum of understanding with the district attorney general; the person does not plead guilty and is not found guilty. On successful completion the charges are dismissed, and under T.C.A. § 40-32-106(d)(1) the person may then petition for expunction of the public records where the charges were dismissed as a result of successful completion of a pretrial diversion programme pursuant to §§ 40-15-102 through 40-15-107. The provision is permissive as to filing and mandatory as to nothing: a petition is required and expunction is not automatic. Section 40-32-106(d)(3) requires the appropriate clerk's fee under § 8-21-401, so unlike a straight dismissal this route is not free. Section 40-32-106(d)(2) bars expunction where the diverted offence was a sexual offence or a violent sexual offence as defined in § 40-39-202. The TBI certificate under § 40-32-102(c) is required here, because the exemption for § 40-32-106 expunctions is expressly carved back where the expunction resulted from successful completion of pretrial diversion. Venue: Statewide statute with originating-court venue. The petition goes to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action — the county criminal, circuit or general sessions court where the case originated. A person with cases in several counties files separately in each. There is no statewide participant form, so what varies locally is the clerk's own paperwork: the AOC directs filers to check with the court clerk because separate forms may be required for multiple charges. Destination: The county criminal, circuit or general sessions court having jurisdiction in the previous action — Confirmed on 2026-08-06 by direct inspection of both Tennessee AOC form indices: the self-help forms page publishes only divorce and order-of-protection forms, and the full forms-and-publications inventory covers appellate, divorce, general sessions civil, mediation, non-IV-D child support, order of protection, parenting plan and trial court forms, plus licensing forms. No expunction form appears in either. This is a negative finding established by inspection of the authoritative index, not by failure to search. filing: A petition to the court having jurisdiction in the previous action, filed with that court's clerk. A separate petition is required in each county. fees: A clerk's fee applies. Section 40-32-106(d)(3) requires the appropriate clerk's fee pursuant to T.C.A. § 8-21-401 for destroying the records, which is the asymmetry a participant should be warned about: diversion is a non-conviction outcome but it is not free, whereas a straight dismissal is. The amount is set by § 8-21-401 and no figure is quoted here. feeWaiver: No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears in the reorganized §§ 40-32-106 to 40-32-110. The TBI operates an unpublished indigency procedure for its separate diversion certificate fee, requiring a form signed by the judge that it supplies on request and does not publish. No waiver mechanism for the clerk's expunction fee was identified. notice: The clerk serves the petition on the district attorney general in the ordinary course. service: Through the clerk. The participant does not effect service. participantSignature: The petitioner signs the petition. notarization: Not prescribed. Confirm the statutory citation with the county clerk or district attorney general before every filing. Chapter 32 was reorganized by Public Chapter 268 of 2025, effective 2025-04-24, and codified by Public Chapter 608, the 2026 Code Bill, effective 2026-03-25. Clerks and published guidance may still use the pre-reorganization numbering: the Tennessee AOC's own expunction page is titled to say updated information is coming to reflect changes to T.C.A. § 40-32-101 and still reasons from that section, which since 2025-04-24 has been nothing but a definitions section. A generated petition citing the wrong section is a rejection risk either way, so the packet is built to carry the current citation with the superseded one noted, and instructs the participant to confirm before filing. A petition is still required after diversion. Completing diversion dismisses the case but leaves it visible until a separate expunction petition is filed, and this is the second most common Tennessee misunderstanding after the not-automatic point. The order of expungement is marked Suspension of Prosecution § 40-15-105 for a pretrial diversion case, which is how the TBI records it. The marking requirement is part of the court's instrument rather than the participant's. Expunction is not automatic. A dismissed charge or a completed diversion stays on background checks until a petition is filed. This is the most common Tennessee misunderstanding and the packet leads with it. No reach to federal records; a diversion guilty plea may remain visible on clearance checks. Sexual offences as defined by the sex offender registry statute can be diverted but cannot be expunged. Section 40-32-106(d)(2) bars expunction of a diverted case on that ground, so a person can complete diversion on such an offence and still be unable to clear the record. This must be in the diversion copy. Exclusion: A diversion that was not successfully completed. Where the diversionary period is not completed the sentence goes into effect and the offence is not expunged. Exclusion: An offence that was a sexual offence or a violent sexual offence as defined in T.C.A. § 40-39-202. Section 40-32-106(d)(2) bars expunction of a diverted case on that ground even though the offence could be diverted, which is the trap that catches people who completed diversion and are still stuck. Exclusion: A dismissal that did not follow diversion, which routes to the free non-conviction petition instead and carries no clerk's fee. Waiting period — Trigger: Successful completion of the diversion programme and dismissal of the charges. There is no further waiting period, but a petition is still required and nothing happens without one. Waiting period — TBI certificate: Required on this route. The § 40-32-102(c) exemption for § 40-32-106 expunctions does not apply where the expunction resulted from successful completion of diversion, so the court must obtain and attach the certificate before entering the order. Waiting period — TBI transmission: The court sends the order to the TBI within 30 days of entry. Manual completion: The state control number Manual completion: The petitioner's signature and date Manual completion: Capture the state control number early. The order cannot be completed without it, and it comes from the TBI criminal history.
